old: Unit 27: Clinical Empiricism, Epidemiology & Medical Ethics
new: Unit 27: Disease, Prevention and Medical Ethics

old: The development of medical science is the triumph of observation, empirical statistics, and sanitary prophylaxis over superstition and entrenched academic hierarchies. Ignác Semmelweis, the 'savior of mothers', revolutionized clinical epidemiology through the rigorous identification of etiologic infection transmission in mid-19th century Vienna and Pest.
new: This unit is about how a disease is explained and prevented: naming the cause of an infection, describing a measure, setting evidence against an old belief, a doctor's duties, and judging the size of a change.

old: In this unit, centered on Semmelweis Ignác's monumental treatise 'A gyermekágyi láz kóroktana' (1861), you will master the elevated academic register of clinical pathology, epidemiological causality, antiseptic protocols, bioethical responsibilities, and medical paradigm shifts at the C1 level.
new: The unit ends with a text about Semmelweis Ignác and childbed fever in Vienna in 1847.
